Schedule 1-hour bench test for ~50 QPS with sample dataset week of 2027-04-26

action_items: Jordan Lee: Share pricing spreadsheet and pilot contract template - due 2027-04-25
Priya Raman: Prepare benchmark config and sample invocation scripts for LangChain and LlamaIndex - due 2027-04-24

summary: Initial technical discovery focused on network integration options for CinderBays compliance requirements. Key concerns were VPC peering, on-prem option for sensitive workloads, gateway/proxy pattern, SDK support for LangChain and LlamaIndex, quota controls, and observability hooks. Agreed to run a small bench and exchange architecture docs.
transcript:
Meeting header
- Date: 2027-04-21
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Participants: Jordan, Priya, Samir (Redwood); Alex, Mei, Daniel, Priya K (CinderBay)

Auto-summary: initial infra and security discovery; pilot planning; follow-up items enumerated

00:00:00 Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining we know your teams are evaluating a few different serving patterns so we wanted to cover hosted dedicated and our private vpc offering and specifically how the gateway or proxy layer would look in your stack
00:00:17 Alex (CinderBay): cool yeah thanks jordan on our side im alex vp eng. we run a mix of public cloud services and some sensitive payment flows that must stay inside our network. main ask is do we need to go on prem for that or can the vpc offer be enough
00:00:36 Mei (SRE): and second, we heavily use langchain and a small subset of llamaindex for retrieval augmented generation. we need native sdk support or easy adapter patterns so our infra doesnt get messy
00:00:50 Priya (Redwood SE): totally makes sense. briefly to align redwood hosted is the fastest path, redwood dedicated is reserved gpu pools for predictable throughput, and redwood private is the VPC/on prem option that gives you network isolation and customer-managed control plane. quick note audio transcription sometimes says redwood privy thats just the auto-captioner
00:01:12 Daniel (Security): ha noted. ok security story first: we need audit logs pushed to our SIEM, KMS integration for key management, and SOC 2 reports. can those be exposed in the private deploy?
00:01:28 Priya (Redwood SE): yes the private deployment supports KMS integrations and audit log forwarding, weve done forwarders to Splunk and Datadog. for the on prem package we can run the control plane behind your firewall and write logs to your ELK. we will share the compliance packet after the call
00:01:48 Alex: good. now on the gateway: our pattern today is a lightweight API gateway that proxies to multiple model endpoints and adds auth, rate limiting, and per-tenant quotas. does redwood expect us to run a sidecar or do you host the gateway? whats the recommended pattern
00:02:06 Samir (Redwood SE): most customers do a small edge gateway in front of Redwood, that can be our recommended proxy template. you can also use direct SDK clients from backend services, but the gateway is useful for centralizing quotas and observability. we have a reference gateway repo that couples with our SDKs and includes rate limit hooks
00:02:29 Alex: reference repo sounds useful. is it opinionated for langchain or does it support LlamaIndex adapters too
00:02:38 Priya (Redwood SE): it has examples for both. for langchain we provide a thin client that implements the LLM API spec; for llamaindex you can use the connector pattern, weve seen two patterns: translate requests to our REST completions endpoint or run a small shim that does chunking and embeddings calls. well send samples
00:02:57 Mei: what about quotas and per-route throttling. we need burst protection and per-team budgets plus token caps per request. can those be enforced at the gateway without adding latency
00:03:12 Samir: yes we expose per-route config, per-api-key quotas, and token-based accounting. the gateway can reject early on quota exceed so latency is minimal. theres also a server-side enforcement so even if someone calls the backend directly the quotas are applied on the platform side
00:03:30 Daniel: any hard limits on QPS per model for dedicated pools? our traffic can spike to 150 qps for short bursts
00:03:38 Priya (Redwood SE): bursts are handled by autoscaling on dedicated but you should size a baseline. for 150 QPS wed recommend reserved pool with burst capacity or a hybrid: hosted for spiky non-sensitive traffic and private for regulated flows
00:03:55 Alex: hybrid pattern might be easiest. we want to keep PII workflows inside private. question on traffic routing: is there a policy engine to route by customer tier or by latency region
00:04:08 Samir: yes the smart routing policy can route by region, model variant, or cost-tier. you can set fallbacks so if the private pool is saturated it can route to a hosted compatible variant with redaction rules applied
00:04:24 Mei: redaction rules how mature are those. we prefer automatic pii redaction for fallback responses
00:04:31 Priya (Redwood SE): we have configurable filters and token scrubbing for sensitive fields; fallback responses can also be flagged and logged separately for audit. we should work on a short runbook for your fallbacks
00:04:45 Alex: switching to sdk integration, our backend services are in go and node. do you have first class sdks or do we call rest endpoints
00:04:58 Jordan (Redwood AE): we have official sdks for python, node, and go is community but supported. the sdks support streaming, function calling, and structured outputs. for node we have examples with langchain-js and puppeteer style wrappers for async streams
00:05:16 Mei: if go is community can you share patterns for using the raw rest API with langchain-style orchestration
00:05:23 Samir: yes youll get templates. common approach is to use the rest endpoints for completions and embedding calls and keep the orchestration in your app or a thin adapter. for llamaindex specifically we recommend doing preprocessing for indexing locally and then using our embeddings API for vector store population
00:05:43 Alex: observability hooks are important. we need per-request trace ids, logs including latency/token breakdown and the ability to link costs back to feature flags. whats available out of the box
00:05:56 Priya (Redwood SE): console exposes per-token cost breakdown, latency histograms, and per-route dashboards. you can also push spans to your tracing backend via open telemetry. theres an ingest hook that adds correlation ids to the token accounting so you can tie cost to request ids
00:06:14 Daniel: ok auditability question. for private deployments can we retain raw transcripts for 90 days and have a delete policy?
00:06:22 Priya (Redwood SE): retention is configured by you in private deploys. default backups exist but you control retention windows and deletion. we can sign an addendum for retention policy in the pilot contract
00:06:34 Alex: model considerations. we currently rely on an open model and occasionally experiment with proprietary variants. can we pin model versions and do canary rollouts
00:06:44 Samir: yes model pinning and rollouts are supported. you can do canary percentages, route a subset of traffic, and have automatic fallback if a rollout fails health checks
00:06:58 Mei: about benchmarks, for our RAG pipeline latency at 3rd percentile matters. can you recommend a test harness or sample prompts and token distributions
00:07:09 Priya (Redwood SE): well provide a bench harness with synthetic token distributions plus a sample dataset for retrieval. well instrument p99 and p3 metrics. for RAG we usually simulate chunking and embedding latency to be realistic
00:07:25 Alex: cost side, how do we estimate token spend given our embedding-heavy pipelines. do you provide cost per embedding unit and tooling to approximate monthly run rates
00:07:36 Jordan (Redwood AE): yes our pricing sheet has per-token and per-embedding units. we can run a cost model against your traffic patterns once you share them. also Optimize has suggestions like batching and quantization recommendations to cut unit costs
00:07:50 Daniel: if we go private on prem what are the ops responsibilities vs redwood. we prefer to keep network and keys but have redwood manage runtime updates
00:07:59 Priya (Redwood SE): typical split: you manage infra and networking, we manage runtime patches and model updates if you opt-in. there is an air gap install option where we hand over an artifact bundle for offline deployment with a clear upgrade path
00:08:16 Alex: good to know. now a practical question about the gateway proxy: do we run it inside our VPC and it forwards to redwood over peered link, or do you deploy a connector into our network
00:08:29 Samir: both are possible. the lightweight reference gateway is run in-customer VPC and talks to our endpoints over private peering or vpn. for high compliance customers we can deploy a connector that stays within your network and only exchanges metadata with the control plane
00:08:46 Mei: latency to model endpoints is a concern. do you provide regional endpoints for private deployments
00:08:53 Priya (Redwood SE): yes private can be regional. with dedicated we put reserved pools in the region you choose which keeps egress low and latency tight. well map your critical regions during the pilot scoping
00:09:06 Alex: can you summarize a recommended pilot for us
00:09:11 Jordan (Redwood AE): recommended pilot: 2-week bench using private VPC connecting via peering, run a 50 qps synthetic workload with your RAG prompts, use langchain and llamaindex adapters, measure p3/p99 latency, enforce quotas via gateway, and validate audit log forwarding. deliverables: bench results, cost model, and a deployment runbook
00:09:33 Priya K (Product): for success criteria we want below 400ms p50 on generation for non-PII flows, ability to keep PII flows inside private with audited logs, and an initial tco estimate for 3 months of pilot traffic
00:09:48 Jordan: perfect we can do that. Samir will own the bench config. Priya will own compliance docs. ill send the pricing and contract template
00:09:58 Alex: ok what about rate limits during the bench. we want to test bursts without service degradations for control-plane failures
00:10:08 Samir: bench will include spike tests. well simulate connection disruptions and autoscale recovery. also include negative tests for quota exceed and fallback routing
00:10:18 Mei: small thing- our tokenization uses a custom preprocessor, will that break streaming or function calls
00:10:26 Priya (Redwood SE): probably not, but we should test. the SDK streaming supports chunked inputs. if youre doing custom tokenizer steps youll want to test how we account tokens. we can add instrumented logs to show token counts per request
00:10:41 Alex: how do we handle secrets and keys for the gateway. do we store them in our ksm or do you store them
00:10:48 Daniel: ksm typo meant kms
00:10:50 Samir: recommended is to store keys in your KMS and use short-lived tokens for the gateway. with private deployment the keys stay on your side. for hosted we use customer-managed keys via envelope encryption where possible
00:11:04 Alex: any gotchas with langchain integrations that youve seen
00:11:09 Priya (Redwood SE): common gotcha is using naive retry logic with streaming which can duplicate tokens; another is not batching embedding writes which bumps cost. our examples include safe retry and batching patterns
00:11:23 Mei: question from security, do you support SSO and role based access for teams inside our org
00:11:28 Jordan: yes SSO with SAML/OIDC and RBAC is supported for dedicated and private. hosted supports SSO too but enterprise RBAC is better in dedicated/private
00:11:39 Alex: what about per-tenant isolation if we onboard multiple internal teams; can we set quotas per internal team and pin model variants
00:11:47 Samir: yes per-api-key quotas and tenant-level policies allow that. you can pin variants per tenant and set cost alerts per key
00:11:56 Priya K: legal proc note: whats the typical lead time for private deployment and do you require an initial commit
00:12:03 Jordan: private on-prem lead time depends on your infra readiness; typical is 6-10 weeks for air gap installs, 2-4 weeks for VPC deployments. Dedicated reserved pools need chartering for capacity but pilot can be faster. we can include a short term pilot without long commit
00:12:19 Alex: ok timeline works. ill take the lead on org paperwork and share a security contact for the SOC2 packet
00:12:28 Mei: one more thing, we use a homegrown vector store. will the embedding format be compatible
00:12:34 Priya (Redwood SE): embeddings are standard floats; we provide norms and update guidance for quantized stores. if your store expects a specific dimensionality we can match it with our embedding models or run a transform step in the gateway
00:12:50 Alex: quick note on costs: if we batch aggressively and quantize for local use, can we keep a single smaller dedicated pool and still maintain low latency
00:12:59 Samir: yes batching and quantization reduce unit compute. Optimize can recommend quantization profiles based on your workload. there are tradeoffs on quality but for many retrieval tasks it works well
00:13:14 Jordan: ok circling back next steps recap
00:13:17 Jordan: action items ive recorded: ill send pricing and pilot contract, priya r will share bench scripts, samir will prepare the gateway reference and peering diagram, alex will send traffic patterns and compliance contact
00:13:31 Alex: sounds good. can we also get a short video walkthrough of the gateway repo so our infra team can onboard quickly
00:13:38 Priya (Redwood SE): yes will record a 20 minute walkthrough and post it to the repo link. expect that with the docs
00:13:46 Daniel: one minor risk is procurement timelines, we may need a minimal legal schedule in parallel. can you provide standard terms earlier
00:13:54 Jordan: yes ill ask legal to provide the standard pilot terms, nothing fancy, and share concurrently with pricing
00:14:02 Mei: transcription note, the auto captions chopped some technical names in an earlier email maybe its fine here
00:14:08 Jordan: ha yeah the captioner is not perfect
00:14:12 Alex: ok thanks everyone. we should reconvene after the bench results. ill aim for a follow-up 30-45 minute sync the week after the bench completes
00:14:21 Jordan: great thanks for the time
00:14:23 Meeting ends

Post-call notes:
- We noticed customer asked explicitly for 90 day transcript retention and KMS control; mark as high priority for legal and compliance packet.
- Customer prefers hybrid model: private for PII, hosted for non-PII spikes.
- Pilot scope agreed: 2-week bench, 50 QPS synthetic with RAG dataset, langchain and llamaindex paths tested, audit log forwarding to customer SIEM.
